name: Mattenai
title: Priest who sent away his foreign wife
summary: Mattenai is a name mentioned several times in the Old Testament, most notably as one of the priests and Levites who had taken foreign wives during Ezra's time. In connection with Ezra's reforms, Mattenai committed to sending away his foreign wife to restore covenant faithfulness to God.

keyEvents.title: Mattenai among the priests with foreign wives
keyEvents.description: Mattenai is mentioned among the sons of Jeshua who were among the priests that had taken foreign wives and committed to sending them away.

keyEvents.title: Mattenai among the sons of Hashum
keyEvents.description: Another Mattenai is mentioned among the sons of Hashum, who also had taken foreign wives and committed to sending them away.

keyEvents.title: Mattenai among the sons of Bani
keyEvents.description: Yet another Mattenai is mentioned among the sons of Bani, who had taken foreign wives during the exile period and the rebuilding.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's reforms against mixed marriages
keyEvents.description: Ezra led a major reform in which the Israelites were required to send away their foreign wives to preserve covenant faithfulness. Mattenai was among those who followed this command.

keyEvents.title: Mattenai mentioned among the priests in Nehemiah's time
keyEvents.description: A Mattenai is named as a head of a priestly family in the days of Joiakim, in connection with Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem.
